Measurement / Baseline Condition: 30-day pre-flight seated resting morning average HR (± 5 bpm)
Watch Condition: Resting HR < 50 bpm or > 90 bpm (or ±15 bpm baseline)
Act-Now Condition: Resting HR < 40 bpm or > 120 bpm (or off-exercise > 160 bpm)
Watch Action: Rest and repeat the pulse reading with good sensor contact. Check symptoms and record the trend.
Act-Now Action: Stop strenuous work, summon the crew medical officer, and assess symptoms immediately.
Escalation Level: Conditional; per rule branch and symptoms
Physiological Rationale: Cardiovascular deconditioning, fluid shift, dehydration, or acute arrhythmogenic stress
Notes: QA 2026-11-14: Resting HR <50/>90 and <40/>120 are stated as validated astronaut limits; not substantiated by general NASA standard. | Keep proposed baseline thresholds as DEMO ONLY; severe symptoms, consciousness and confirmed signal take priority over number.

Measurement / Baseline Condition: 14-day pre-flight standardized morning 5-minute seated resting rMSSD baseline
Watch Condition: Trend: RMSSD >20% below same-person baseline across repeated quality-checked readings (DEMO rule)
Act-Now Condition: NO STANDALONE HRV EMERGENCY RULE. Escalate based on serious symptoms or another independently verified risk.
Watch Action: Repeat HRV under standardized quiet conditions; review recent sleep, exertion and symptoms.
Act-Now Action: Do not activate an emergency solely from HRV. Escalate immediately if serious symptoms occur.
Escalation Level: Conditional; per rule branch and symptoms
Physiological Rationale: Provisional marker of cumulative autonomic strain and allostatic load; non-diagnostic for acute autonomic collapse alone.
Notes: QA 2026-11-14: 20% and 50% drops cannot establish severe autonomic collapse or be standalone emergency criteria. | Use repeated baseline deviation as a nonurgent trend flag; no independent Act-now from HRV alone.

Measurement / Baseline Condition: Individual pre-flight resting room-air SpO₂ average (typically 97%–99%)
Watch Action: Check sensor placement, repeat the reading and assess breathing and cabin oxygen conditions.
Act-Now Action: Call the crew medical officer immediately for persistent low oxygen readings or breathing difficulty; follow approved medical/atmosphere procedures.
Escalation Level: Conditional; per rule branch and symptoms
Physiological Rationale: Arterial desaturation, pocket hypercapnia, toxic inhalation, or atelectasis
Notes: QA 2026-11-14: 90–94 and <90 are general clinical screening values, not verified ISS-specific safety limits; oximetry can misread. | Confirm measurement quality; urgent symptoms or repeated low SpO2 warrant immediate onboard assessment; do not infer CO2 from SpO2.

Measurement / Baseline Condition: 30-day pre-flight resting seated brachial blood pressure average
Watch Condition: Repeated cuff SBP 130-139 or DBP 85-89 may prompt routine review; PPG BP class cannot be equated to mmHg
Act-Now Condition: Extreme cuff BP >180/120 WITH serious symptoms, syncope or severe clinical concern -> immediate crew medical response; 160/100 without symptoms requires prompt review, not automatic hypertensive emergency.
Watch Action: Obtain a calibrated cuff reading if available; recheck and record symptoms.
Act-Now Action: Escalate immediately for serious symptoms with extreme BP or fainting. Do not diagnose an emergency from a PPG class.
Escalation Level: Conditional; per rule branch and symptoms
Physiological Rationale: Differentiates operational precaution (≥160/100 mmHg) from AHA-defined hypertensive emergency (>180/120 mmHg with target-organ symptoms).
Notes: QA 2026-11-14: 160/100 is not synonymous with hypertensive emergency; PPG category is not an oscillometric cuff measurement. | Distinguish operations caution from emergency; >180/120 WITH concerning symptoms requires urgent assessment; verify with cuff.

Measurement / Baseline Condition: Pre-flight 24-hour Holter ECG recording documenting normal sinus rhythm
Nominal Condition: Normal Sinus Rhythm (NSR), HR 60–100 bpm, < 1 PVC/hour
Watch Condition: Isolated PVCs/PACs (> 5/min) or transient sinus pauses
Act-Now Condition: Sustained VT, rapid AFib, or frequent polymorphic PVCs
Watch Action: Repeat the measurement; notify the crew medical officer about recurrent irregularity; obtain ECG if available.
Act-Now Action: For syncope, chest pain, severe breathlessness or sustained abnormal rhythm, activate the emergency response.
Escalation Level: Conditional; per rule branch and symptoms
Physiological Rationale: Myocardial irritability, autonomic shifts, electrolyte imbalance, arrhythmogenic risk
Notes: QA 2026-11-14: PPG irregularity is screening, not ECG diagnosis; PVCs/min and VT labels require ECG. | Use irregular-pulse flag prompting repeat and clinician review; serious symptoms trigger urgent protocol.

Measurement / Baseline Condition: Pre-flight standardized LBNP profile (-30 to -40 mmHg) or 10-minute active stand test baseline
Nominal Condition: LBNP/Stand: HR increase < 20 bpm; SBP change between -10 and +10 mmHg
Watch Condition: HR increase > 25 bpm or SBP drop 15–20 mmHg during LBNP (orbit) or standing (1g)
Act-Now Condition: SBP drop > 30 mmHg, HR > 130 bpm, or presyncope / syncope during LBNP or standing
Watch Action: Stop the test if dizzy, secure against falls and report symptoms; do not apply free-float standing thresholds.
Act-Now Action: If presyncope or syncope occurs, activate the collapse/urgent assessment protocol.
Escalation Level: Conditional; per rule branch and symptoms
Physiological Rationale: Impaired baroreflex sensitivity, post-flight orthostatic intolerance, presyncope; LBNP in microgravity, stand test in gravity.
Notes: QA 2026-11-14: Active standing is impossible in free-float microgravity; LBNP is not interchangeable with standing test. | Specify condition: surface gravity/after landing vs LBNP in orbit; require adapted references and no automatic clearance.

Measurement / Baseline Condition: 14-day pre-flight circadian resting core temperature profile (24h cycles)
Watch Action: Repeat measurement with the same device and method; assess exertion, symptoms and habitat temperature.
Act-Now Action: Notify the medical officer for severe symptoms or confirmed dangerously abnormal temperature.
Escalation Level: Conditional; per rule branch and symptoms
Physiological Rationale: Elevated resting setpoint ('space fever'), impaired convective cooling, infection/sepsis
Notes: QA 2026-11-14: 'Space fever' does not mean all high readings are infection; sensor types differ. | Confirm method, site and exercise context; severe systemic symptoms trigger urgent assessment.

Measurement / Baseline Condition: Pre-flight baseline fasting capillary glucose (average of 3 morning draws) and HbA1c
Watch Condition: Glucose <70 and >=54 mg/dL (ADA Level 1); repeated high values require contextual assessment
Act-Now Condition: Glucose <54 mg/dL (ADA Level 2) or severe cognitive/physical impairment requiring assistance at ANY glucose level (Level 3); marked hyperglycemia plus serious symptoms needs immediate assessment.
Watch Action: Confirm the glucose reading and contact the crew medical officer; follow the approved low-glucose care procedure.
Act-Now Action: If confused, unresponsive, seizure-like, or markedly low glucose, immediately summon help and use approved crew medical kit procedures.
Escalation Level: Conditional; per rule branch and symptoms
Physiological Rationale: Provisional marker of cumulative autonomic strain and allostatic load; non-diagnostic for acute autonomic collapse alone.
Notes: QA 2026-11-14: Updated <70 and <54 values align with ADA classes, but severity depends on symptoms and context; >250 alone does not prove DKA. | Use ADA low-glucose categories with correct measurement and urgent assessment for altered mental status; no automatic drug/dose.

Measurement / Baseline Condition: NASA nutritional prescription based on BMR and individual body mass
Watch Condition: Caloric intake < 80% target or fluid < 2.0 L/day for 2 days
Act-Now Condition: Caloric intake < 50% target for > 3 days or severe fluid deficit
Watch Action: Review intake and hydration against individual plan; inform nutrition/medical crew if deficit persists.
Act-Now Action: Notify the medical officer if severe dehydration, inability to eat/drink, or concerning symptoms occur.
Escalation Level: Conditional; per rule branch and symptoms
Physiological Rationale: Chronic negative energy balance accelerating muscle wasting and bone loss
Notes: QA 2026-11-14: Fixed 2,500–3,200 kcal and 2.5L are not universal prescriptions; low intake alone not emergency. | Use astronaut-specific prescription; watch sustained deficits; urgent escalation depends on clinical dehydration/illness.

Measurement / Baseline Condition: Pre-flight 14-day actigraphy and subjective sleep diary baseline
Watch Condition: Sleep < 6.0 hrs/night for 2 nights or efficiency < 75%
Act-Now Condition: Sleep < 4.0 hrs/night for ≥ 2 days or 24h acute sleep loss
Watch Action: Review sleep conditions and schedule; avoid high-risk tasks while significantly fatigued.
Act-Now Action: Arrange immediate crew safety review if unable to remain alert for a critical activity; this is not itself a diagnosis.
Escalation Level: Conditional; per rule branch and symptoms
Physiological Rationale: Circadian desynchrony, sleep fragmentation, neurobehavioral vigilance decay
Notes: QA 2026-11-14: Sleep <4h two nights is a task-safety escalation, not an emergency diagnosis. | Use fatigue and task-safety restrictions pending crew evaluation; no automated prescription.

Measurement / Baseline Condition: Pre-flight neurobehavioral evaluation baseline score across standardized domains
Watch Condition: Score drop ≥ 2 points below baseline for 3 consecutive days
Act-Now Condition: Survey score ≤ 3/10, acute panic crisis, or severe distress
Watch Action: Offer confidential check-in, workload adjustment and optional support contact.
Act-Now Action: If immediate safety or severe psychological distress is reported, alert the crew medical officer under the privacy/safety protocol.
Escalation Level: Conditional; per rule branch and symptoms
Physiological Rationale: Confinement, isolation, operational stress, psychological third-quarter phenomenon
Notes: QA 2026-11-14: One 1–10 survey is not a validated clinical screen; <=3 does not diagnose acute psychiatric crisis. | Select validated brief instrument, include privacy and direct red-flag symptom checks; do not infer disease from a score.

Measurement / Baseline Condition: Pre-flight standardized 3-minute PVT-B baseline mean response speed (1/RT) and lapse frequency
Nominal Condition: Mean RT: 200 – 250 ms; 0 – 1 lapses (≥355 ms) per 3-minute trial
Watch Condition: 3-minute PVT-B decline from individual baseline (15% or >2 lapses only DEMO threshold)
Act-Now Condition: No validated medical emergency cutoff from PVT-B alone; stop critical tasks and assess when markedly impaired.
Watch Action: Repeat in standardized conditions; review fatigue and cabin environment.
Act-Now Action: Pause safety-critical tasks if performance is markedly impaired; request crew assessment.
Escalation Level: Conditional; per rule branch and symptoms
Physiological Rationale: Assesses sustained attention and vigilance fatigue; utilizes validated PVT-B 3-min protocol with ≥355 ms lapse threshold.
Notes: QA 2026-11-14: PVT-B 3-minute cutoffs are not proven EVA safety limits; platform/device effects. | Use PVT-B matched scoring and personalized trend; proposed 15%/35% thresholds only simulated.

Measurement / Baseline Condition: Pre-flight VO2max evaluation and 1-rep maximum (1RM) resistive loading profiles
Nominal Condition: Aerobic: ≥ 30 min/day at 70–85% HRmax; Resistive: 100% prescribed ARED
Act-Now Condition: Prescribed exercise missed for ≥ 3 consecutive days
Watch Action: Review the planned exercise program and equipment access.
Act-Now Action: Notify medical/rehabilitation staff for inability to exercise due to injury or concerning symptoms.
Escalation Level: Conditional; per rule branch and symptoms
Physiological Rationale: Musculoskeletal and aerobic deconditioning from mechanical unloading
Notes: QA 2026-11-14: Missing 3 days of activity is not an acute medical emergency. | Treat adherence as rehabilitation plan review, not urgent surgery/cardiac treatment.

Measurement / Baseline Condition: Pre-flight serum CTX and calcium panel drawn during baseline medical exam
Nominal Condition: Serum CTX: 0.15 – 0.55 ng/mL; Total Calcium: 8.5 – 10.2 mg/dL
Watch Condition: Bone resorption markers (serum CTX) > 25% above baseline
Act-Now Condition: Serum CTX > 50% elevation or hypercalcemia (> 10.5 mg/dL)
Watch Action: Repeat at the specified sample time and assay; arrange planned crew medical review.
Act-Now Action: Urgent response only for concerning clinical symptoms; isolated biomarker change is not an emergency.
Escalation Level: Conditional; per rule branch and symptoms
Physiological Rationale: Uncoupled bone remodeling, rapid cancellous resorption, hypercalciuria/nephrolithiasis
Notes: QA 2026-11-14: CTX 25/50% changes do not alone indicate acute fracture or kidney stone; assay-specific ranges. | Trend assay-specific CTX/P1NP with flight surgeon; acute concerns require symptoms/other tests.

Measurement / Baseline Condition: Pre-flight resting cytokine baseline and viral antibody titer panel
Nominal Condition: IL-6: < 5.0 pg/mL; TNF-α: < 8.0 pg/mL; Normal leukocyte differentials
Watch Condition: Cytokine deviation vs own baseline (30% is DEMO ONLY); symptoms and assay consistency required
Act-Now Condition: NO STANDALONE CYTOKINE EMERGENCY RULE. Escalate for severe symptoms or other verified medical red flags.
Watch Action: Interpret with symptoms and validated lab-specific reference ranges; monitor per medical plan.
Act-Now Action: Activate immediate assessment for serious infection symptoms; avoid diagnosing infection from cytokines alone.
Escalation Level: Conditional; per rule branch and symptoms
Physiological Rationale: Cytokine alterations reflect systemic stress or immune modulation; changes are nonspecific and require clinical correlation.
Notes: QA 2026-11-14: IL-6/TNF changes are nonspecific; doubling cytokines cannot diagnose infection or 'immune collapse'. | Do not use isolated cytokine elevations as emergency trigger; incorporate symptoms and other tests.

Measurement / Baseline Condition: Cumulative lifetime radiation exposure record maintained by NASA Radiation Health Officer
Nominal Condition: Background in LEO: 0.3 – 0.8 mSv/day (< 1.0 mSv/day nominal)
Watch Condition: Mission radiation warning / rising dose relative to mission-specific limits; 1mSv/day DEMO ONLY
Act-Now Condition: Active spacecraft solar-particle-event or radiation shelter alarm (mission-defined); 10mSv/h is NOT an acute radiation syndrome diagnostic cutoff.
Watch Action: Verify the environmental alert and mission-set radiation constraints; review shielding/EVA status.
Act-Now Action: Follow the spacecraft's authorized solar-particle-event shelter warning and suspend EVA as directed.
Escalation Level: Conditional; per rule branch and symptoms
Physiological Rationale: Operational storm shelter trigger during solar particle events; distinct from clinical ARS which requires high absorbed doses (>0.7 Gy).
Notes: QA 2026-11-14: 10 mSv/h should not be labelled ARS cutoff; mission limits depend on organ, duration, mission. | Use spacecraft radiation-alert and storm-shelter signals with mission-set limits, not a universal 10 mSv/h ARS rule.

Measurement / Baseline Condition: Vehicle ECLSS baseline environmental limit specification (NASA-STD-3001 Vol 2)
Nominal Condition: Cabin ppCO₂ < 2.0 mmHg (approx. < 2,600 ppm); nominal < 1.5 mmHg
Watch Condition: Operational early warning at ppCO2 >=2 mmHg (DEMO CONSERVATIVE) or rising trend
Act-Now Condition: One-hour average cabin ppCO2 >3 mmHg violates NASA-STD-3001 Rev F nominal requirement [V2 6004]; environmental response per mission-specific procedures. Do not label 4 mmHg as CO2 narcosis.
Watch Action: Verify CO2 sensor, duration and local ventilation; notify life-support operators.
Act-Now Action: Activate authorized environmental response for mission CO2 alarm or symptomatic crew; do not equate 4 mmHg with CO2 narcosis.
Escalation Level: Conditional; per rule branch and symptoms
Physiological Rationale: Operational environmental threshold to prevent mild hypercapnic symptoms (headache, SANS); clinical CO₂ narcosis occurs at much higher levels.
Notes: QA 2026-11-14: NASA 2026 Vol2 Rev F specifies 1-hour habitat average <=3 mmHg; 2/4 are not validated medical severity categories. | Label 2 mmHg as conservative engineering warning only; 3 mmHg 1-hour requirement, off-nominal response mission-specific.
